Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

regcompR 0.1.0

  • First release.
  • summary_param() reparameterizes a family by its mean, mode, geometric or harmonic mean; uplift() and qini() (equal to tools4uplift) for uplift models; skovgaard_test() gives Skovgaard’s modified directed likelihood ratio r* (equal to likelihoodAsy::rstar()).
  • Inference: vcov(type = "HC1") to "HC3" (equal to sandwich::vcovHC), boot_regcomp() (parametric and case bootstrap, clustered), power_sim() (power by simulation), vuong_test() and best_subset(); step_regcomp() and best_subset() also use AICc and Hannan-Quinn.
  • Random effect structures relmat() (known relatedness matrix), car(), leroux() and icar() (areal models; icar() plus an iid term is BYM) and spacetime() (separable Leroux by AR(1)); exact normal marginal likelihoods checked against direct computation.
  • Econometrics: iv_regcomp() (two stage least squares with weak instrument, Wu-Hausman and Sargan tests; equal to ivreg), panel_within() (fixed effects within estimator; equal to plm) and hausman_test() (equal to plm::phtest).
  • Families: huber (its ML estimate with fixed scale is the Huber M estimate of MASS::rlm), stochastic_frontier (normal minus half normal), multinomial_probit (independent errors) and partial_odds() (partial proportional odds; equal to ordinal::clm with nominal effects).
  • Nonlinear formulas: y ~ nl(expr) with a formula for each nonlinear parameter (covariates and random effects allowed) for any family, fitted by engine = "ml" (equal to nls() and to lme4::nlmer()) or by Stan.
  • Reporting: regcomp_table() builds regression tables of one or several fits (rows grouped by distribution parameter, random effect standard deviations and correlations, fit statistics, optional standardized or exponentiated coefficients and sandwich or quasi standard errors) that print in the console and render in R Markdown and Quarto (HTML, PDF, Word). tidy(), glance() and augment() methods work with broom and modelsummary. export_table() writes .csv, .html, .tex, .md and .docx; export_plot() saves any diagnostic plot; coef_plot() draws estimates of several fits.
  • Inference: anova() likelihood ratio tests of nested fits, wald_test() for linear hypotheses, simple_slopes() and johnson_neyman() for moderation, interaction plots through plot(which = "effects", by = ), vif() generalized variance inflation factors, and step_regcomp() stepwise selection by AIC or BIC.
  • Effects: avg_effects() (average marginal effects and contrasts, with delta method or posterior uncertainty), marginal_means() (average predictions at covariate values), r2() (McFadden, Cox and Snell, Nagelkerke, and Nakagawa marginal and conditional R squared) and icc().
  • vcov(type = "quasi") and summary(vcov = ) give quasi-likelihood (Pearson dispersion) standard errors, matching quasibinomial and quasipoisson.
  • Dirichlet regression (matrix response; one log linked concentration per component) and the shifted lognormal family.
  • person_period(cuts = "events") builds Cox risk sets: a Poisson fit reproduces coxph() with Breslow ties exactly, and random effects give Cox frailty models.
  • family_capabilities() (formerly capabilities(), renamed so that attaching the package masks no base R function) labels family specific numerical methods "algorithm", separately from closed forms ("analytic") and the generic fallback ("numeric").
  • scoring_rule(re = "marginal") scores the predictive law of a new group, mixing over draws of its random effects. cv_regcomp(group = ) now scores held out groups this way by default (previously with the effects set to zero; re = "zero" restores that) and clusters the standard error by group.
  • The multivariate hypergeometric law takes the number of draws size.
  • Finite difference scores and Hessians respect joint parameter constraints.
  • Truncation, censoring, rounding, monotone transformations, splicing, CDF generators, convolutions (including two laws that both have point masses) and copulas now accept continuous laws with point masses; copula margins may also differ in type (a count and a continuous amount, say).
  • regcomp_control(init = ) sets initial values for the Stan runners.
  • Registry of 278 distribution families with densities, distribution functions, quantiles, random generation, moments and references.
  • Distributional regression by maximum likelihood with a Laplace approximation for random effects and smooths, through TMB (RTMB), and by Bayesian inference in Stan, JAGS and OpenBUGS.
  • Random effects in any parameter with nested, crossed, structured (AR(1), compound symmetry, unstructured, Ornstein Uhlenbeck, spatial kernels) and multiple membership terms.
  • Ordinal, nominal, bivariate binary and sample selection models.
  • Operators for inflation, hurdles, truncation, censoring, mixtures, compounding, convolution, splicing, cure models and copulas.
  • Generalized estimating equations, cluster robust covariances, exact Poisson regression, quantile regression for counts and person period expansion for discrete time hazards.
  • Residuals, scoring rules, cross validation, model comparison and plots.
